scope.decoder: jpeg-js 0.4.4 as pinned in the current lockfile
scope.target: Decode supported 16 MP JPEG to full-resolution width*height*4 RGBA within the 256 MiB utility-process PeakWorkingSet64 target.

findings.finding: The pinned jpeg-js decoder copies the encoded input, creates an Int32Array(64) for every coefficient block, retains full-image component scanlines, materializes an RGB intermediate, and then allocates the final image output. formatAsRGBA=false still leaves the caller responsible for constructing full RGBA; useTArray only selects the typed-array container.

The current production preflight estimates coefficient blocks, component lines, RGB/RGBA output, encoded-input copies, JPEG tables and process reserve before entering jpeg-js. Lowering its estimate would admit more decodes without reducing decoder allocations.

The 16 MP, 20 MiB synthetic JPEG runs after preflight were capacity-rejected before full decode: five 4:4:4 samples peaked at 101.55 MiB and five 4:2:0 samples peaked at 101.30 MiB. Those rejection measurements do not establish successful 16 MP JPEG support.

Earlier one-sample preflight-disabled measurements peaked at 246.86 MiB for a 4 MP 4:4:4 JPEG and 242.73 MiB for a 6 MP 4:2:0 JPEG. These near-budget single samples do not justify weakening the guard or prove a hard limit.

recommendation: Keep the current preflight. A materially lower peak while returning complete 16 MP RGBA requires a substantial streaming/reworked decoder or a separately approved decoder route; do not infer acceptance from capacity-rejected samples. Any selected route still needs repeated fresh-worker Windows measurements, independent pixel comparisons, supported JPEG sampling/progression and metadata fixtures, cancellation/failure coverage, and packaged-worker verification.
notVerified: Successful full-resolution 16 MP JPEG decode within the 256 MiB process target.
A universal memory ceiling across JPEG inputs, progressive JPEG, metadata, and packaged full-app execution.
Approval or installation of an alternative decoder, including its complete distribution/license review.
